defects.description: The registry key is the trimmed handle lowercased but never Unicode-normalized, so a decomposed spelling and a precomposed spelling of the same name are two keys, and two members hold handles that render identically although the README promises one entry per handle whatever its normalization.

trigger.expected: D1 claim(NFD 'Zürich') then claim(NFC 'Zürich') -> second=threw handle taken: Zürich entries=1 renders=@Zürich
trigger.actual: D1 claim(NFD 'Zürich') then claim(NFC 'Zürich') -> second=ok "Zürich" entries=2 renders=@Zürich,@Zürich

defects.why_missed: Every handle in the suite is typed in one normalization form, so the key function is exercised only where trimming and lowercasing are enough and the two spellings never meet.

defects.description: The reserved comparison folds the handle with toLocaleLowerCase in the dashboard's locale, so in a Turkish deployment I folds to a dotless ı and ADMIN no longer equals the reserved admin, and a reserved name is claimable.

trigger.expected: D2 new Registry({ locale: 'tr' }).claim('ADMIN') -> threw reserved handle: ADMIN entries=0
trigger.actual: D2 new Registry({ locale: 'tr' }).claim('ADMIN') -> ok "ADMIN" entries=1

defects.why_missed: The case test only runs the default en-US locale, where locale-dependent folding and language-independent folding agree on every handle it tries, so the locale parameter never changes an outcome.
